name: turnstile
whenToEnable: Stop bots at credential-entry and form-submit points without asking real users to prove themselves. Stacks a Cloudflare Turnstile humanity check on any route — magic-link and OTP login, signup, lead capture, contact. dev and staging wire Cloudflare's test keys automatically, a feature deployment resolves the same pair by default, and only `prod` provisions a real widget. The widget secret is stored and read through @pithy-sh/secrets, so the secrets capability is required.
scaffold: `turnstile({ ... })` in pithy.config.ts declares a visible widget, which gates `login` by default. Add an `invisible` widget and `protect` entries (action → mode) for silent forms. Social/OAuth login is never gated.

Ensure the secrets capability is provisioned (`pithy add secrets` then `pithy secrets provision`) — the turnstile widget secret is stored and read through @pithy-sh/secrets, which the secrets capability sets up.

Run `pithy turnstile provision`. Until it runs, the sitekeys are blank and sign-in is blocked. It writes Cloudflare's documented test secret for dev (into the dev secrets file) and staging (into the staging secrets store), provisions the real prod widget with its secret in the prod secrets store, and writes every environment's public sitekey into this `turnstile({ ... })` block. The build inlines them, so redeploy afterward.

Stack the gate on a route: `import { turnstile } from "@pithy-sh/turnstile/src/http/middleware"` and `app.use("/signup", turnstile())`. It reads the token from the `cf-turnstile-response` body field (or a header) and resolves the secret through @pithy-sh/secrets. Render the widget on your front-end with the public sitekey — Pithy ships no front-end component.

configOptions.describe: The widget login renders. `pithy turnstile provision` writes each environment's sitekey here, and the build inlines it.
